boxes.meaning: to treat someone to a meal or drink

english.note: Use 請 as the all-purpose spoken choice for inviting someone over, treating them to something, or politely asking people to do something.
Use this when buying something means treating someone to a meal, drink, or gift.

examples.english: I’ll invite you for a cup of coffee.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 ceng2 nei5 jam2 bui1 gaa3 fe1

examples.english: This time, I’ll buy you dinner.
examples.jyutping: gam1 ci3 ngo5 ceng2 nei5 sik6 faan6

english.note: Use 請 as the everyday all-purpose verb for taking someone on as an employee.
Use this for engaging or hiring a person to work, rather than for engaging a space or machine.

examples.english: The company will employ a new accountant, who will start work next month.
examples.traditional: 間公司請咗個新會計，佢下個月返工。
examples.jyutping: gaan1 gung1 si1 ceng2 zo2 go3 san1 wui6 gai3 keoi5 haa6 go3 jyut6 faan1 gung1

examples.english: We’ll engage a new manager for the shop.
examples.traditional: 我哋會請個新店長返嚟。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 wui5 ceng2 go3 san1 dim3 zoeng2 faan1 lei4

english.note: Use this polite verb when requesting someone to do something, as in 請你坐低.

examples.english: I politely request that you sit down first.

english.note: Use 請 when asking someone to attend an event or inviting them somewhere.

examples.english: I want to ask you to come to my birthday party.
examples.traditional: 我想請你嚟我個生日會。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 ceng2 nei5 lai4 ngo5 go3 saang1 jat6 wui2
